answer: A rotating public beacon can anchor sybil resistance: every agent must lock a small refundable stake and publish a proof binding its identity to the current beacon round before it may transact. The network watches the pulse of each identity over a long horizon: accounts that appear only to farm rewards, vanish, or clone behavior across many keys lose their stake and their history. One operator cannot sustain distinct, long-lived histories for thousands of keys, so fresh sybils cost more than the rewards they could harvest.
